minutes.headline: Finance Committee heard police, fire and land use budget briefings; fire chief floated a fourth shift, no votes except adjournment.
minutes.summary: The committee opened budget season department briefings with the Police Department, Fire Department and Land Use, with new members welcomed. The fire chief proposed a fourth shift, and a long discussion followed on ambulance receipts, free cash and whether a revolving or enterprise fund is possible. The only vote was adjournment.

public_comment.topic: Chair asked for public comment at the start; none on Zoom.
Asked why the police switched from a patrol K9 to a drug-sniffing dog and suggested one multi-purpose dog rather than separate comfort and K9 dogs.
Praised both chiefs, urged the town manager to make the fire fourth-shift proposal happen, and said he does not support the new town hall proposal.
Commended the fire chief's honest answer that a fourth shift would not simply save overtime.

votes.motion: Motion to adjourn; all in favor, chair said it passes.

budget_items.what_was_said: The police secured ARPA funds for 30 body cameras to replace failing four-year-old units. The chief said future replacement will likely need a capital plan as grants run out.
A state earmark funded a virtual use-of-force training simulator now in service.

budget_items.topic: Police FY25 spending to date and prior-year spending
budget_items.what_was_said: The police budget is partway through the year with some lines trending high; prior years were mostly expended with surpluses from vacancies.

budget_items.topic: K9 stipend for comfort dog handler
budget_items.what_was_said: Chief requested an incentive increase so the comfort dog handler receives the same K9 care stipend as the patrol K9 handler.
The lease increased and now covers maintenance.
Insurance on the patrol K9 is cheaper than potential vet bills.
Lockup level funded and much lower than before the Sheriff's safekeep program.
The town's assessment for regional dispatch could change as other towns' allocations shift.
Increase without dispatch and including dispatch were stated, about a 1.2 increase; dispatch figures may change.
No salary reserve in the police budget; any settlement would come from the town-level salary reserve.
Grant funding was pulled back by the state and the position could not be filled at the offered pay.

budget_items.topic: Fire FY25 salaries and EMS expense
budget_items.what_was_said: Salaries are on target but extra was spent on open per diem shifts; EMS expense continues to run over.
Contractual increase in salaries and a requested increase in overtime.
Rates were raised in September but most patients are on government insurance so revenue gain is limited.
Estimated cost of adding a fourth shift in one year, which could be phased over up to three years.
Training four call staff cost the town roughly this amount, with buyback agreements.
Requested additional funds for advanced life support supplies.
Requested additional funds for department software.
Requested increase to a line unchanged since before 2010; radios cost several thousand each.
Proposed FY26 capital replacement of the 10-year-old prevention vehicle.
ARPA covered an ambulance and equipment for the fire department.
A state grant funded protective clothing dryer, thermal cameras and gear.

budget_items.topic: Federal AFG grant for brush truck
budget_items.what_was_said: A federal grant application for a brush truck would need a small town match; outcome unknown.
State grants for fire education each year.
Ambulance receipts go to the general fund and flow into free cash; the estimated yearly amount and rate increase were stated.
Chief stated the overall fire budget increase percent.
A member asked for the sources of last year's certified free cash; the town manager will provide it and said free cash should not fund operations.

decisions.decision: Ambulance receipts, revolving/enterprise fund options to be reviewed, with the town manager to provide detail and the topic kept for a later meeting after budget season.
Town manager agreed to provide a breakdown of sources of certified free cash within about a week.
Police staffing plan to be reassessed by the chief and new town manager.
Committee will need further discussion and targeting on the fire fourth-shift proposal once the preliminary budget is presented.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee heard opening budget briefings from the Police Department, Fire Department and Land Use; no votes were taken except adjournment.
The fire chief proposed a fourth shift, and the committee said it will need further discussion once the preliminary budget is presented.
Members discussed ambulance receipts and whether a revolving or enterprise fund is possible; the town manager is to provide detail, with the topic held until after budget season.
The town manager agreed to provide a breakdown of the sources of certified free cash within about a week.
The police staffing plan is to be reassessed by the chief and the new town manager, and a state-funded mental health co-responder position could not be filled.

why_it_matters: A fourth fire shift and any change to how ambulance receipts are held would affect the fire budget and the town's reliance on free cash, and so could shape what residents are asked to approve at town meeting.
Grant and earmark money paying for police equipment, such as body cameras, is running out, so replacement costs may move into the regular budget or a capital plan.
